analysis: What changed vs the 7 AM brief: the rally strengthened into mid-morning — Nasdaq +5.72% to +7%, S&P +4.06% to +5.3%, Dow +2.44% to +3.2% — and is on track for the best day since April 2025, but the tape already shows the first wobble: indices peaked at the open and eased, with SPY opening at 724.30 and trading 720.62 (+4.47%) by 9:56 AM ET. NVDA extended from +30% to +32-34% (~$166-169 vs Friday's $125.53 close), and the Trump angle firmed up: Trump told CNBC Monday he spoke to Nvidia's board and vouched for Huang, corroborating Semafor's report that he called the board hours before the vote; a reinstatement petition topped 180,000 signatures including Elon Musk. New confirmed deal flow: Amazon announced it will buy Decart's Optimization Stack technology and hire its founders/team (~$7.5B reported by Bloomberg/Calcalist; Amazon disclosed no terms), the third big AI M&A signal in two days after CrowdStrike-Zscaler. The morning's data did not dent the rally: S&P Global flash PMI cooled to a four-month low of 54.6 (services 54.7, below the 55.8 consensus) but stayed in expansion and consistent with ~3% Q4 GDP. Community mood is split, not euphoric: the HN thread on the reinstatement passed 1,500 points and 1,280 comments, while r/wallstreetbets discussion fractured into gains-posting vs rug-pull/manipulation claims, with the board's whiplash (unanimous removal 11 days ago, 'no return' a week ago, unanimous reinstatement now) drawing credibility questions. What did NOT change: Capital Economics ('dead cat bounce') and BCA ('failed to find a floor') are still fading the move, the SEC accounting probe, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline and Huang's Dec 1 House testimony remain open, and Anthropic is flat around $89 — the rally is broad in AI hardware and megacaps but still selective. Signal vs noise: the reinstatement (8-K filed), the Amazon-Decart confirmation and the breadth of the chip rebound are signal; the size of the open's pop is noise until the close in a thin Thanksgiving-week tape, and the pullback off the open's high is the first real test of whether buyers hold.

headlines.headline: Rally holding into mid-morning but off the open's peak: S&P +5.3%, Nasdaq +7%, Dow +3.2% (CNN, ~10:45 AM ET), on track for the best day since April 2025. SPY opened at 724.30 and traded 720.62 (+4.47%) by 9:56 AM ET; QQQ +6.56%, DIA +2.62%, IWM +2.87%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce strengthened vs the 7 AM print, but indices peaked at the bell and eased — the first sign of whether buyers hold the gains into the close in a thin holiday week.

headlines.headline: Nvidia extended its surge to +32-34% in morning trading (~$166-169 vs Friday's $125.53 close; IBD had +34% to $168.89). Trump told CNBC Monday he spoke to Nvidia's board and vouched for Huang's character; a petition calling for reinstatement drew 180,000+ signatures including Elon Musk. Arm CEO Rene Haas — reportedly approached in the CEO search — announced he is staying at Arm with a contract extension through 2033.
headlines.why_it_matters: The political backing is now on the record via CNBC, not just the board statement — and the leadership vacuum is fully closed with the reported successor candidate staying put; this is the engine of the whole AI rebound, six days after the Nov 17 earnings call where the chair ruled out Huang's return.

headlines.headline: Amazon confirmed it will buy AI startup Decart's Optimization Stack technology and hire its founders and engineering team; the deal is subject to regulatory clearance. Amazon disclosed no financial terms; Bloomberg reported the value at about $7.5B and Calcalist/Globes reported more than $7.5B, paid in cash and stock in installments with founders staying five years. The tech is aimed at making Amazon's Trainium/Inferentia chips run AI models faster and cheaper.
headlines.why_it_matters: A second confirmed Big Tech AI deal in a day after CrowdStrike-Zscaler — dealmaking is continuing through the drawdown, and Amazon is paying up to loosen Nvidia's grip on AI infrastructure; the $7.5B figure is reported, not confirmed by Amazon.

headlines.headline: AI breadth stayed wide: Tesla +11%, Alphabet +6-7%, Meta and Microsoft +4% each (Investopedia/IBD); chip stocks Marvell, Micron and Intel each +12%+, SOXX +11% and memory ETF DRAM +19% after both plunged 10%+ on Friday; Dell +17%, CoreWeave and Nebius +28% each, Lumentum +19%+.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound is not just Nvidia — semis, neocloud and megacaps are all lifting together, which is what a durable bounce needs; the open's peak is the level to watch for follow-through.

headlines.headline: S&P Global flash November PMI: composite 54.6, a four-month low (from 55.9 in October); services 54.7 vs 55.8 expected (from 56.1); manufacturing 54.5 (from 54.9, in line). S&P Global said the survey remains consistent with about 3% annualized Q4 GDP growth; hiring stayed strong and inflation pressures persisted (Reuters/ActionForex).
headlines.why_it_matters: Growth cooled but stayed in expansion and missed only on services — a soft landing read that did not dent the rally, and it keeps the near-certain December Fed hike on track.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) is little changed around $89 in morning trading after fading its premarket gain at the open (it opened at $93.65, touched $94.24, then fell to $87.73 by 9:54 AM ET; Friday's close was $88.91).
headlines.why_it_matters: The newest mega-IPO is sitting out the relief rally after Friday's 8.5% drop — a reminder buyers are still selective and IPO euphoria has not returned.
